title: How Trump Is Wielding Power to Stifle Speech
partialText: President Trump has harnessed agencies across the government to curtail press freedoms, a sweeping campaign that free speech advocates say will have lasting effects.

title: Trump Says Irish Unification Would Be ‘Fantastic,’ Breaking With Precedent
partialText: The United States has been officially neutral on an issue that was a source of decades of violence in Northern Ireland until a 1998 peace deal.

title: Visa Issue Threatens U.S.-Brazil Cooperation on Crime
partialText: Officials say the Trump administration is blocking some of Brazil’s efforts to expand cooperation on fighting transnational crime.

title: Anthropic C.E.O. Dario Amodei Calls for A.I. Slowdown
partialText: In a 3,800-word essay, Dario Amodei laid out the rapidly advancing capabilities of artificial intelligence and said there needed to be greater safety controls across the industry.

title: Inside the Discussions at AI Companies Over a Superintelligence Doomsday
partialText: Researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google are increasingly trying to raise awareness about the risks of artificial intelligence.

title: Why It’s Difficult for Tech Companies to Rein In A.I.
partialText: Researchers say artificial intelligence is developing faster than the systems put in place to monitor and control it.

title: Iran Finds Escalation Is Fruitful Path to Leverage in War With U.S.
partialText: Iran and its allies now hold sway over two key oil shipping routes, and Tehran is setting the stage for a diplomatic win that could enhance its stature.

title: Saudi Arabia’s Oil ‘Lifeline’ Was Attacked. Here’s What to Know.
partialText: A drone attack from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to close its East-West pipeline, the kingdom said, threatening a key workaround to Iran’s Persian Gulf blockade.

title: ‘We Left in the Clothes We Were Wearing’: Yemenis Flee New Fighting
partialText: Hunger and disease have tormented Yemen for years. Now, fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Iran-backed Houthis is pushing it to the brink.

title: Why Mokha, Historic Port That Shaped the Coffee Trade, Is a Prize in Yemen’s War
partialText: A strategic location on the Red Sea afforded the city centuries of trading dominance — and makes it a coveted target in today’s fighting in the Middle East.

title: Ohio Republican in Key Senate Race Fires Campaign Aide, Citing Social Media Photo of Nazis
partialText: Senator Jon Husted dismissed his political director because of activity displaying a “complete lack” of judgment, according to a spokeswoman.

title: Inflation Complicates Trump’s Midterms Pitch to Voters
partialText: Gas prices are high, mortgage rates are climbing and inflation remains well above target, complicating the president’s midterm appeal.

title: Republicans, Facing Midterm Peril, Try to Brand Democrats as Communists
partialText: Communism, in the president’s hyperbolic telling, is a graver threat to the country than the Pearl Harbor or 9/11 attacks were. Whether this midterm strategy works is an open question.

title: Republican Groups Rush to Paxton’s Aid in Texas After Staying on Sidelines
partialText: An organization allied with Senate G.O.P. leaders has booked more than $51 million in ads. Now, Ken Paxton has a financial edge after months of being outspent by his Democratic rival.

title: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor Say the End of the World Is Now on the Table
partialText: In a new book, the writers argue that a powerful coalition of “end times fascists” is just fine with the earth’s demise.

title: Moldova Has to Choose Between Russia and Europe
partialText: Moldova is a fault line in a new geopolitical reality.

title: Trump Catastrophically Miscalculated in Georgia
partialText: The president incubated the career of one of his greatest critics.

title: Walk This Way
partialText: Are there everyday activities that you can turn into a walk?

title: Manhattan Bus Lane Plan for 34th Street May Be Stuck in Gridlock
partialText: Months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city would proceed with a redesign of 34th Street that had been halted by the Trump administration, the plan is no closer to completion.
